utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today, we are Wednesday, the 8th of October, 2008. I would like to greet all the people present in the courtroom; Mr. Ferrara, who is leading the witness, Mr. Mundis, as well as all the people assisting them in the courtroom. I shall also like to greet Mr. Seselj, and in a few moments I shall greet the witness when he walks into the courtroom. I seize this opportunity to ask the Registrar to give me the countdown and tell me how much time Mr. Ferrara has had so far. Very briefly, a housekeeping matter: I would like to tell Mr. Mundis that the Trial Chamber intends to resume its hearings as of Tuesday, the 6th of January, onwards. The winter recess lasts after that. In other words, we would resume our hearings during the winter recess period. As you know, the Judges have decided to use the courtrooms whenever they are available, and this might occur during the winter recess, which will be the case for this trial. We can therefore resume on the 6th of January quite smoothly, which means that we would stop calling witnesses as of the 15th of December. This is what I wanted to tell you so that you can adjust your witnesses schedule accordingly. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that the 7th of January is Serbian Orthodox Christmas, and I demand that we do not work on that day because we, honourable and honest Serbs, celebrate Christmas in prison on that day, the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem. We can then sit on the following Friday. That is not a problem. We cannot have a hearing on the 7th of January. We would resume on the 6th of January, have no hearing on the 7th, and have a hearing on the 8th and 9th of January. That is not a problem. Let's bring the witness in now and ask him whether he has done his homework. Mr. Ferrara, you will then have to ask him whether he has completed the chart and how many names he has identified, because I assume you are going to ask to have the document tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the countdown is concerned, the Registrar has just told us that you've had one hour and fifty-six minutes, so you have one hour and four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give the floor to Mr. Ferrara now.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, before going to the list we gave to the witness, I feel yesterday we forgot to request to tender into evidence the article -- the press report we discussed at the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right. Registrar, can we have an exhibit number for the press article.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor has to explain what makes this newspaper article relevant. It's not an interview with the witness. If it were an interview with the witness, I wouldn't mind at all. However, this is an OPED [phoen] article and we haven't heard the journalist who wrote the article, so how can we admit it into evidence? If we can take for granted everything that is published in the newspapers, then there will be no end to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, according to the case law of the Appeals Chambers and the Trial Chambers, we can admit documents, even if the author of the document in question is not present. All that is needed are elements in this document that can be linked to the indictment, in terms of relevance and probative value. There needs to be a degree of some probative value. You would like to respond, Mr. Ferrara?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree with you, and I want to highlight something else. During the testimony of Witness VS-61 concerning the same part of the indictment, the Hrtkovci case, the Trial Chamber showed its interest in what was reported at the time in the local and the international press. I remember that the Presiding Judge pointed out the importance of this press article. I have here exactly the quote of the hearing of the 25th of September, 2008. For the reference of Mr. Seselj, the transcript is 100 to 113, 100 to 24 [sic], and for this reason the Prosecution has created a press package that is included in the court binder sent to the Trial Chamber and to the accused, containing numerous press articles related to the events occurred in Hrtkovci in May 1992. All these articles were published from May to August 1992, except one that is an interview with the accused on the same matter. It was published on 19 July 1993. They are all related to the intimidation and expulsions of the Croatian population and non-Serbian population in Hrtkovci, and my request is to tender all these documents into evidence. I can give the 65 ter number of these articles. For the record, the first one is 1350, 1524, 1544, that is the one we discussed yesterday, 1878, 1309, 1310, and the last two are two documents, number 7270 and 7272. That's not -- are not still added to the Prosecution exhibit list. My request is to add these new documents to the Prosecution exhibit list, due to the relevance and probative value, and to tender into evidence the entire package. THE COURT: I shall confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, the document we saw yesterday, which is document 1544, well, the Trial Chamber decides to admit this document, and we shall ask the Registrar to give it an exhibit number, because we feel that it is relevant to some degree and there is a link, as one says in English, and this may have some probative value. However, the other documents, 1350, 1524, 1878, well, I think we need to address these documents in the presence of the witness. Now, we shall give an exhibit number to this one document for the time being. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 1544 will be Exhibit number P550.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: We'll discuss these documents later with the witness, Your Honours. Just for the record, I want to repeat the transcript reference that I don't see in the transcript. It is the hearing 25th September 2008. The transcript page is 10021, line 13; 10022, line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, did you read the list that you received yesterday from the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, I have read it several times, and I'm facing a bit of a dilemma. Your Honours, by your leave, I wish to address a request -- or, rather, I have a remark to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask the OTP, for the sake of expeditiousness, when they send documents to me and when they put questions to me in relation to something like this, I think that we lose time in this way. It's a bit too voluminous. There's a lot of information contained here, over 700 numbers, and the list is annex 11, "Hrtkovci, known victims." Now, what does "known victims" mean? Are these victims of physical abuse, mistreatment, or victims of psychological abuse and violence? Also, could a question be put to me more specifically in relation to a particular name and surname and a particular address, who was exactly meant? This way, I'm facing a dilemma. I've read a lot of names that are the same, the same last names, entire families. I can tell by the last names that some of them are in Hrtkovci to this day. As for destination, a lot are missing, and I know that many of these people are still in Hrtkovci, they still live there. So is this a list of victims of psychological violence or physical torture only, such as ejection and so on? I also added a few names that I'm aware of persons who are not on this list. Finally, my own name is on the list, and I will explain in relation to that addition, what persons this has to do with and what it is that happened to them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, we have a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I apologise, because maybe yesterday my question was not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When you say "known victims," the indictment concerning Hrtkovci is an indictment for persecution, so the known victims are victims -- people who were forced to leave Hrtkovci in 1992 because they were expelled or because they were maltreated and so on. So when we say "known victims," and the expert will recommend this list and they will tender the report, of course we'll be more clear on this point. We intend -- people that were forced leave Hrtkovci, so this is the main question, if you know that some of the people on this list were forced to leave Hrtkovci in 1992, and of course it's possible that they were forced -- they were able to come back later on at a time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a very serious objection. I mean, all of my objections are serious, but this one is particularly serious. Mr. Ferrara, counsel for the Prosecution, referred to the content of the indictment and the crime of persecution that I have been charged with. I believe that it is indispensable for it to be explained to the witness what the crime of persecution is in accordance with Article 5 of the Statute of the ICTY. This witness is not a lawyer. He's certainly os not aware of that. The crime of persecution is very specifically spelled out and defined, and it has to do with specific actions that constitute persecution or actions of a similar nature which are identical in terms of intensity to those mentioned, because here the witness is brought into a situation to explain himself and interpret what he means by "persecution." For example, yesterday, if Rade Cakmak said something to a man at the meeting of the Council of the Local Commune, this person took this to be an insult, a threat, and then he left Hrtkovci. That is not persecution. There is a crime that is persecution, and if you ask the witness about that, then you have to explain to him what is meant by "persecution" in accordance with the Statute of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, can you explain to the witness, in simple words, what the accused has just talked about? He said in his list that some people were still there, so there might be mistakes in the list. He doesn't quite understand the difference between those people who left of their own free will, those people who were forced to leave, and those who were encouraged to leave because they were afraid, and that would come under the heading of "Persecution." That is difficult for a lawyer and even more difficult for someone who is a farmer. So could you explain this to him in a simple fashion, what it is exactly you expect from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. As I say, I think the best is to be clear is to read exactly to the witness what the accused has to face on this part of the case, so it was the indictment related to Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 33, that's it. I assume that the OTP should pay me for helping them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: We'll see what can we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, don't try and be witty.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, the accused, in paragraph 33 of the indictment, "in May 1992, Vojislav Seselj came to Vojvodina and met with associates in the SRS. He instructed these associates to contact non-Serbs and threatened them with death if they did not leave the area." "On 6 May 1992, he gave an inflammatory speech in the village of Hrtkovci, calling for the expulsions of Croats from the area, reading a list of individual Croat residents who should leave for Croatia. "As a result of this speech, a number of Croat residents decided to leave Hrtkovci. After the speech, supporters and associates of the accused, including members of the SRS and the Serbian Chetnik Movement, began a campaign of ethnic cleansing directed to non-Serbs, particularly Croats in Hrtkovci. "During the next three months, many non-Serbs were harassed, threatened with death, and intimidated, forcing them to leave the area. Houses of Croats were looted and occupied by Serbs. Serb families were being displaced from other parts of the former Yugoslavia, often occupied the homes of those Serbs who had been compelled to leave. By his participation in these acts, Vojislav Seselj committed deportation, a crime against humanity, inhuman acts, that is, forcible transfers, a crime against humanity as well." Now, is it clear to you what kind of a crime Mr. Seselj is accused of concerning your village? And so I repeat my question: In this list that you have read, do you know some people who were forcibly expelled from Hrtkovci or who were -- who decide to leave Hrtkovci due to the threats that they received in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the honourable Prosecution, now the question is clear to me. I can only circle a few numbers or, rather, a few names here and a few names that I've added myself. The names that I added are: "Bagi, Josip; Tkalac, Jelica; Tkalac, Franja; Pakic, Vlado; Pakic Rosalija." I put circles around the following: Vuksanic, Branko and Vuksanic, Nikola; the village doctor and his father. Another person, Fumic, Marko. The other persons from this list, I can just say that I know their last names and, I can say that it is true that most of the persons on this list carried out an exchange and went to Croatia or even beyond, further abroad. That is my response to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you tell us these other names of these persons that carried out an exchange?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, those people that exchanged property, I don't know whether you know this or not, which ones were the ones that voluntarily exchanged their property without being influenced by anything, and those that decided to carry out an exchange because they had to? Are you able to make the difference? I'm telling you this because in 1991, 1992, in the beginning, some people may have felt that in light of the situation, in light of what might happen, it might be better to leave without anybody asking them to leave in any way. These people left of their own free will. Were there any of these or not? Only you can tell. Are you able to make this difference or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, and I do have information that there are persons who carried out voluntary exchanges at the very beginning. Later on, everything that happened was either under duress, or out of fear, or the motive was the following: "My friends left, my family left, so I'm going to leave too." I'm aware of two examples from the very beginning of persons who did this voluntarily. That's the Jogar [phoen] family. I think they carried out an exchange for a property in Zagreb. Now Ulemek, Nikola is the owner. He works on waterworks maintenance in the local commune. He confirmed that as well. Also, I know from earlier on, from the daughter of the -- rather, the daughters of Mr. Jogar lived in Zagreb earlier on, so that led him to sell his house, and he had this opportunity to carry out an exchange. And then there's the family Olidenko [phoen]. That man's daughter also lived in Zagreb earlier on. So these are the first two persons that I am aware of who carried out an exchange voluntarily. I believe that everything else was done either out of fear or under different types of threat. I have no specific evidence, hard evidence, except for a few cases where I was personally present; namely, Fumic, Marko, then Tkalac, Zenica, Franja. Specifically, as far as Marko Fumic is concerned, he had been attacked and threatened by death. The police recorded this and certain action was taken. Tkalac, Zenica, and Tkalac, Franja, they also carried out an exchange, but earlier on their house had been attacked. A grenade had been thrown at their front door, facing the street. A few persons who had been tortured physically remained, nevertheless. I know the family -- well, they're related to me, too. It is Jozika, my wife's brother, Bagi, and this family that I also added to the list. They were thrown out and attacked physically: Pakic, Vlado; Pakic, Rosalija. To this day, they lived in Hrtkovci, but for a few days they were out of their house. There is a police record of that, too. The police stopped the culprits from stealing things from them, and then they were returned to their home. That is what I can confirm in relation to this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Concerning this Marko Fumic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to move in closed session because I want to use a document coming from the Serbian Archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You can continue, Mr. Ejic.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Marko Fumic case, I know the following: On that day, I went to visit his brother, Milan. I had business dealings with him. It was towards the evening, and in front of the house of Marko Fumic I noticed that there were two or three police cars parked and a policeman or two in front of his house. When I went to his brother, Milan, Marko came a bit later. He told him that he needed to go to the police station in Ruma to give a statement, and since he needed to go with his own car, and the police was going to drive him in the police car, he needed somebody to drive his own car in order to be able to come back home. His brother couldn't do it because he was busy, he had some other previous engagement, so I offered to do it, which means -- or, rather, Marko told me that he was told to bring the car documents and to have somebody drive his car. At the police station, I waited in the corridor, and I heard from Marko and I also saw an unfamiliar person wearing a camouflage uniform when they went to the bathroom. That's when I saw them. They put some questions to me at the police station. They wanted to know to what extent the village was informed about this event. I answered that I supposed that the village knew about this, because later on I heard that neighbours reported to the police that some unfamiliar people came to visit Marko. It was reported by Dobrosav Markovic and his wife, Violeta. They saw that, they reported it to the police, and then the news spread throughout the village. What seemed striking to me in this note, which I consider not to be correct, was that a sniper rifle was found in Marko's house. It is true that a rifle was found, but it was an air gun. Later on, when Marko left, I bought that rifle off him, and that caused me to have problems as well. This is how I know what kind of rifle he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Maybe there's a misunderstanding, because in the English version the sniper rifle is in the possession of Ostoja Sibincic, because I don't know what you read exactly -- did you read exactly? I read in my version it's Ostoja Sibincic from Hrtkovci was in collusion with them and gave them information on Croatian extremists in Hrtkovci. "He was found in possession." I think "he" is Ostoja Sibincic who was found in possession of a sniper rifle, not Marko Fumic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how it says in the Serbian version as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I then misinterpreted. I thought that it was found in Marko Fumic's house. I hereby correct myself. What I know from Marko Fumic himself, who shortly after these events moved to Croatia, having carried out an exchange, is that they issued a death threat to him on that occasion. They threatened to eliminate him. And even as he was on his way to the bathroom, in the corridor, one of these men threatened him, telling him that he had to move out from Hrtkovci or else he would be eliminated. And then it was done on another occasion as well, since the first one wasn't successful. After this interview, we went to visit a friend who is a lawyer in Ruma and who used to work at the Secretariat earlier, so we explained the case to him and asked for his advice, and he told us that it would be best for him to carry out an exchange because he couldn't guarantee his safety or help him in any way concerning this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While you were answering questions by the Prosecution, I was having a look at the document. I was therefore looking at the document, and I saw the following: There is a whole series of events taking place, and they will trigger the departure of Croats, Croat residents. This document shows that there are individuals carrying out certain actions, and a whole lot of events are being described here. It seems that the local authorities are doing their best, and when the authorities realise that some people are forcibly expelled, investigations are carried out and the judicial authorities take action. This is not chaos, nor anarchy, because judicial authorities take action and decisions are made by judges. The person who wrote this document simply explains that perpetrators were released by the judges due to the issue of refugees, very numerous refugees, and that there may be some reaction from the refugees, so they are released. This report also indicates that members of the Radical Serb Party, for instance, on the 1st June 1992, will play a specific role. Still in that document, members of the Voluntary Serb Guard are referred to, and, for example, on the 11th of May, 1992, they kidnapped several refugees. The report concludes by saying that the behaviour of the members of the Voluntary Serb Guard is problematic. To your knowledge, Witness, who are these people? Who are the members of those -- this voluntary Serb guard, who are they, because it seems that they are playing an important role here, so who are they, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not aware of that, and I think that this information has been made up, that there were no such situations in Hrtkovci. At least I'm not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you saying that it was fabricated, because it's written in that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of that, Your Honours. And I correct myself, the part where I said that it was made up, fabricated. If it says so in the document, I'm simply not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Still in the document, of course, my fellow Judges and myself will review that document more in-depth, but it says that in your area, TO members came, TO members from Krajina. The document indicates that they, too, occupied Croat apartments and so on, and it seems that they also carry out specific actions. This document says that there are paramilitary forces. Again, to your knowledge, did these individuals actually come? This is in the third paragraph before the end of the document. We're in open session. Maybe we should move to private session. Let's move back into private session. Mr. Registrar, let's move back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender into evidence also the list marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the list marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like you to show the list to Mr. Seselj. He needs to have a look at it. Madam Usher, could you please show the list to Mr. Seselj so that he can have a look at the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar tells me that you will receive a copy just after the break, but you will be shown the document right away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once I see this document, I will give you my position. I can't go over it in a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, fine. We'll discuss this again after the break, and during the break a copy will be made available. Mr. Ferrara, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, you mentioned Rade Cakmak. Who is Rade Cakmak? No, you said yesterday "Rade Cakmak." My question is another one. Do you know if Rade Cakmak and/or Ostoja Sibincic were arrested?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I am acquainted with Rade Cakmak, and I know that Ostoja Sibincic, Rade Cakmak and some other people, such as Mirko Paunovic, and I also think the son of Rade Cakmak, that all of them were arrested during the reign of Prime Minister Milan Panic, who ordered them to be arrested due to acts that they committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: For -- do you know the charge?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know was violence towards other persons, instigation of violence, and unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please, can we have on the screen the document bearing the 65 ter number 1615.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you read this document? Not loudly; on your own. Are these the weapons that were found in the possession of Ostoja Sibincic? Do you know it? It is a receipt of a search.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P552.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please, can we have another document on the screen. It is 65 ter number 1610.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, can you read this document on your own? Do you know if these were the weapons that were found in the possession of Rade Cakmak?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that I have only heard that weapons were found on him, but I can't confirm the details contained here, whether they're accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P553.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you know if they were convicted of the crimes charged, Rade Cakmak and Ostoja Sibincic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I know that they were convicted. They spent a long time in detention, too, and that time was taken into account when sentencing them. I heard that Sibincic was sentenced and then that the sentence was suspended. It was a two-year sentence, and that's how long he spent in detention. There were two separate trials. One was concerning violence and instigation to violence, and the other trial was for weapons possession. I don't know about the other case, whether he was sentenced and whether he served the sentence, the other case being the one for firearms possession. That's all I know about these two cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please, can we have on the screen the document bearing 65 ter number 1837.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purposes of the transcript, I'd like to record that this judgement issued by a tribunal describes the conviction and sentences of imprisonment for Sibincic as well as Cakmak. However, such sentences are suspended. In the reasons why these people are being convicted, it is referred to, the unlawful possession of weapons, but there is nothing about political motives. So it seems that what is being described here is individual behaviours, individual conducts. Nothing is said about the wider political context at the time. Nothing to that effect is indicated. However, forcible exchanges of apartments are referred to, but we don't know who's behind all this. At least the judgement remains silent on that issue. So please put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Is this the conviction which you referred to before?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest of the sentence because there is paper shuffling.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is the judgement that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's give this judicial document an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P554.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You say that the arrest of Ostoja Sibincic and Rade Cakmak was ordered by the Minister of Interior, led by Mr. Panic, I think. Do you have a meeting -- did you personally have a meeting to the Minister of Interior to discuss what was happening in Hrtkovci in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. Ferrara is misinterpreting the witness's statement. The witness stated, and I wrote that down, that the then federal prime minister, Milan Panic, issued an order for their arrest or, rather, ordered their arrest. He did not mention any Minister of the Interior or Minister of Foreign Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You're right, it was a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When you refer to this order of arrest issued by the prime minister, how do you know that the prime minister was interested in the arrest of this Ostoja Sibincic and Rade Cakmak?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know he was interested on the basis of what I knew from the public domain, from the media. Also, from the information obtained from a delegation that then visited the Minister for Human Rights, and afterwards the federal SUP, where we presented information about what was going on in Hrtkovci. I imagine that it was on the basis of that information, too, that he ordered the arrest of those persons, Sibincic and Cakmak.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How did you inform the federal SUP?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pero Bjegovic, one of our residents who was a policeman at the federal SUP at the time, he helped us. He made it possible for us to schedule this kind of meeting. I cannot remember exactly who it was that had received us; but I know that we then presented the facts concerning the behaviour of Sibincic and people around him, the violence that was involved, mentioned Rade Cakmak and many other things that were happening at the time in Hrtkovci. A note was compiled concerning all our remarks, and I assume that what followed soon afterwards way this intervention by Mr. Panic to have these two arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When you say "he made it possible for us to schedule this kind of meeting," who participated in this meeting? You, of course, and after?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samo, Nedeljka; Karlac, Vranja; Karlac, Marija; Momic, Slobodan [Realtime transcript read in error, "Milosevic" and somebody else. I can't remember all the names now. Five or six of us attended this meeting. Previously, this group had been to see the minister. I think his last name was Grubac. Then we went to the federal SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's an error -- THE COURT: Mr. Ferrara, one moment. To enable you to get yourself organised, I'd just like to tell you that you have 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, in the transcript, I think one of the participants of the meeting was not Slobodan Milosevic. Maybe in the transcript there is some mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So you say Karlac, and Slobodan, and --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Momic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Who was the minister at the time? Sorry, the minister --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent sure, but Minister Grubac was the Minister for Human Rights or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: And the Minister of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Ivan Stefanac?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. People talked about it, and I know about it from the media too. What happened to him was murder on the road between Hrtkovci and Nikinci. Official proceedings were instituted in relation to this case. He was run over by a passenger vehicle several times, and it was deemed manslaughter. Mijat Stevanac was a resident of Hrtkovci. Before the murder, he lived in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Is it Ivan or Mijat, the first name?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stefanac. I know him by his nickname, "Mijat." Now, whether "Ivan" is his real name, I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, we have already had documents here concerning the trial of his murderers, and on the basis of that we know that his real name is Mijat. The Prosecutor should familiarise himself with all the documents that have been introduced until now, and it is only then that he can continue his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecutor is perfectly familiar. The statement is indicated "Ivan," in the documents it is indicated "Mijat," so it's important for the witness to clarify. Don't worry, Mr. Seselj, about that, the [indiscernible] of the Prosecutor with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can I show you some press articles? Please, Mr. Registrar, please can we have on the screen the 65 ter number 1350. Do you remember this open letter that was written to the residents of Hrtkovci, indicated in this article?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I know that this is my former neighbour or, rather, neighbours, Musa and Branka Jasarevic. I cannot recall all the articles, it's been a long time, hasn't it; but I know what this is written about and I know the persons in the photograph who are described in the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Who is this person in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person that can be seen in the photograph, the first one standing there with a pitch fork, is Musa Jasarevic, and in the back is his wife, Branka. I think the picture was taken at the door of their room or some other part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you know if they were threatened, or were they forced to leave?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about what happened to me, too. I know that on one occasion, two ladies came to see me. They had a small piece of paper in their hands. They said that they got this from Ostoja Sibincic, that the number of this house said that this was a house that was supposed to be exchanged. I laughed and I said, "Where is your house that you want to exchange?" And then mentioned Slatina or something like that, and I said, "Thank you, but that will not do. If you have something in Serbia, then perhaps we can carry out an exchange." They were a bit surprised and they said, "Oh, you're not a Croat?" And I said, "No," and then they apologised and they went further on. As for my neighbour Jasarevic, I heard that there were similar visits that were paid to him. Since they are related to Marko Fumic, I assume that the main motive, in addition to the one that was present in my case, was the fear based on what had happened to Marko. So that is why they opted for an exchange. That is my opinion and knowledge in relation to the Jasarevic family.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P555.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, can we have on the screen the document with the 65 ter number 1524.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you proceed, Mr. Ferrara, can I ask you whether you intend discussing document 7271?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'd like to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Be careful, because the clock is ticking.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that document. I have 7270 and then 7272.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a report stemming from --

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I read this, 7272. I will not talk about document 7271, only 7272.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't wish to discuss it? That's a problem, because as far as the procedure is concerned, I cannot talk about a document which you do not discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document is exactly the part of the beginning of the verdict that I tender it. That's the reason why I don't want to discuss it. In any case, Mr. Seselj is aware of this document because we disclosed it to him on the 1st of October, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj will discuss it; I don't know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what this is all about, Mr. President. I just have here the documents that the Prosecutor had kindly prepared for me for this witness. I cannot keep dragging 6.000 documents around all the time, nor can I remember the numbers of all 6.000 documents involved. I have no idea what this is all about. I have a binder here, and in order to carry less, I took out of the binder the documents that the Prosecutor prepared for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You should have the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, normally speaking, you should have this document, since it is in the binder that has been provided to the Bench. This is an indictment issued by the Ruma prosecutor on the 15th of September, 1992, against Sibincic and Cakmak. That is the document in question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, can you read this article on your own? Are you familiar with the article? Have you read it before, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Let's move, in this case, to the document with the 65 ter number 1309. Mr. Ejic, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot was written in the newspapers. It's been a long time since then. I can't remember everything. I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Which one are you reading; the one below, this one? It has the title "Half of the village ..." in the English. Can you read the end of the article, where you're expressly mentioned? It should be the last paragraph. It's the last column.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it. Yes, I've read it, I've seen my name. I know this document from the press. I remember this, now that I have read it. Now that I have read parts of it, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you give an interview at the time with this statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give an interview. Like many of the persons mentioned here, Dragutin Todorovic and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number P556.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One point of clarification, Witness. Are you of Hungarian descent or -- is part of your family Hungarian or are you Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am a Serb by birth. My father is a Serb and my mother is a Catholic from Bosnia. My way of thinking is not ethnic-based. I'm more of a cosmopolitan person. My wife is an ethnic Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your wife was Hungarian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, my wife is an ethnic Hungarian. THE COURT: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, can we have on the screen the 65 ter number 7270.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you read on your own the first paragraph? It should be -- your statement should be there.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document? Have you given -- did you give the time and interview to this journalist?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of this, and I remember having given this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the document into evidence. This document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P557.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I appreciate your bringing these things to us, but it would be helpful if you would at least draw our attention to the parts of these interviews which are relevant to the issues that we are discussing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the entire article is related to our case, because it's a long list of interviewed people from Hrtkovci that were threatened or were maltreated, were forcible expelled, so of course I'm asking to the witness only the part that he is personally involved with, because he gave this interview, but the whole article related to the events that occurred in Hrtkovci at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what exactly does the articles show; that the witness confirms that people were expelled from Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Is that the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: A corroboration of what the witness is saying today in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have five minutes left before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, can we show to the witness the last press article. It is 7272, the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, this is not an original article at all. This is a copy of the alleged article. Somebody simply copied it, rewrote it. I did not object to the first article, but since you agreed to admit into evidence newspaper articles, I think that the actual articles should be put forth, rather than something that the Prosecutor claims that is the content of the article. We cannot see it on the basis of this. It has to be a photocopy of the article from the newspaper, and then there has to be a translation into Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, what do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't have the original of the article, but it is a transcript, it is indicated the source and the copyright, it is a Chicago Tribune Company and the newspaper is the "Chicago Tribune," so I think it's enough to tender the document into evidence. We have the transcript of the article in the English version, and the translation in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, the OTP received the entire article, and based on that, made excerpts that we have. Is that right, is that how things happened? Don't you have the original article? It must be somewhere with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I will look for it, but I didn't find it by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the excerpts, pages 11 and 12 are mentioned, so this must have been a 12- to 13-page document, I'm sure. Could you see whether you can find it? Please proceed. No, we're going to have the break now, because it is now 10.30. Perhaps you can check and see whether you can find the entire document. In the meantime, I believe you have something like ten minutes left, maximum. You have 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Seselj received the document. Mr. Seselj, do you have any observations on the document regarding the 700 people; 722, to be more specific, plus the 6 that were added by the witness, so 728 in total, those people who would have left from the area? And I believe the Prosecutor has already asked the further document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I fully agree, I fully agree to have this document admitted into evidence, together with the notes made by the witness, because the witness was one of the most influential political figures in Hrtkovci in the relevant period of time, and if he wasn't able to list more than eight names out of a total of over 700, 728, so he circled just eight names of persons who could be said that they left Hrtkovci under threats and so on, then in that light this is, in fact, a Defence exhibit, not the Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P558.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Ferrara, you've provided a copy of the new document; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour -- no, no, no, Mr. Seselj provided this document to use in the cross, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought it came from you. No, it's coming from Mr. Seselj. Fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Regarding these articles, my case manager informed me that we will be able to find probably the original in the afternoon, so we can start discussing it with the witness today and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll see. There will be a hearing tomorrow, so we can continue tomorrow. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, please, can you read this document, this article? Are you familiar with it? Did you give an interview to the journalist of the "Chicago Tribune?" You were mentioned in the second page. Maybe you can move to the second page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it, and, yes, I am familiar with this article. I remember giving this statement to -- to this media outlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will mark this document for identification, and we'll wait for the rest of the document. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI P559.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a short question for you. When you met that American journalist working for this Chicago newspaper, and when you describe all the events which took place for him, when we see the document we can see that some of the things that are described in the article you've also mentioned during your statement, during the answers you've provided, and we also find the same description in other documents. But why didn't the journalist, in his article, why didn't he try and find out who was behind all this? Why didn't he ask you the following: "You've just said that such-and-such events took place. Who are these people?" In the article, armed men are mentioned, but we don't know who they are. During the interview, didn't you know who these people were? When you're a journalist and you want to write an article, of course you want to describe what happened, but then you also want to know who was behind such acts, including politicians, as the case may be. When I take a look at pages 11 and 12 of the article, I can't find this, so my question is: Did the journalist do his job or didn't you know exactly who were the men behind those events or those actions? Sibincic, the famous Sibincic, is mentioned in the article, for instance, and here we are in July 1993, but Sibincic is identified as being a former soldier. We're not saying or we're not reading Sibincic is a member of that particular movement of the Serbian Radical Party and so on. This is not said in that article. So what's your opinion about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I could understand your question, the journalist, who interviewed me as well, did not formulate his questions in those terms, "Who are these armed people, what are their names," and so on. I just told him, in general terms, that I knew that the refugees who had come to our town had weapons that hadn't been confiscated at the border. I think it should have been done. I think that those words of mine were reproduced in the article, and also the kinds of weapons that I had in mind when I said that they were armed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me start again. There are many details in the article, an extraordinary number of details. For instance, Franja Tkalac has his 42-year-old, [as interpreted], we also know who he was married to. There are many, many details, and the more -- the most important thing, which is of course the most important political issue about what's going on. What's going on, well, then the journalist is not interested in that particular issue. And apparently this is a 12-page article, we only have two of them, but it seems that it's a very long article, and of course we need to see what the rest of the article is. And then what you're saying is the journalist didn't ask. I take note of your answer, but I'm quite surprised by it. Let me add that a few names are mentioned, Sibincic among others. It is indicated that he was a former soldier, but of course some other things could have been said about him, although there aren't. That's all I wanted to say, but I wanted it to be recorded in the transcript so that everybody was aware of it. Since I have the floor, I don't want to interrupt Mr. Prosecutor, but a moment ago I was talking about a document which the Prosecutor will not submit. This is a report coming from the Prosecutor, but which has a link with the judgement issued which was admitted. We spoke of that a moment ago, we said both sentences against Sibincic and Cakmak. When a trial takes place, sir, but you know about it, of course, because you were living in that area, when a trial takes place there's first of all an indictment, charges, defined by the local prosecutor. Who's the local prosecutor? In this case, this is the Ruma prosecutor. He prepares an indictment. Looking at the indictment or the list of charges, I see that there is a very specific description of all the events which took place. In particular, in his report he gives names, names of the perpetrators, among which Mr. Sibincic is to be found, and, and I believe this is very important here, the prosecutor describes the offences perpetrated by Sibincic and the others, and he indicates that these were acts against the freedom and the rights of the citizens of other nations or other ethnic groups, and he says this is in violation of Article 61(A), paragraph 1, of the Criminal Code of Serbia. This prosecutor reports to the legal authorities in place at the time. He reports to the judge such offences constituted by crimes with an ethnic connotation, and then he provides a long list of victims. The question that comes to my mind is the following: We have a prosecutor which reports to the power in place at the time. He's pinpointing all the events that are taking place at the time. To your opinion, is the prosecutor doing so on behalf of the Republic of Serbia, because he's in fact an agent of the Republic of Serbia and he's, in fact, expressing his condemnation of what's going on at the time? Now, in your opinion, don't you think that he's trying to show that the authority in place at the time is actually opposed to what's going on? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for putting this question to me. It will be a pleasure to reply. My opinion and that of my many people who submitted criminal complaints against unidentified perpetrators, many of these criminal complaints ended up in the drawers of the prosecution. It is my opinion, and I'm convinced of this based on my own case, is that the prosecutor did not act on behalf of the state in all cases, only when he was forced due to numerous articles and pressures and calls from citizens and their complaints, only when he felt he absolutely needed to do something about it. If you wish, I can further elaborate and confirm my own belief. I will quote my own case. I was once thrown out of commercial premises that I was leasing from the local commune. I was evicted by a group of seven, the majority of whom were members of the Serbian Radical Party. After I was evicted, I went and reported the case to the SUP on the phone, and the person on duty there directed me to contact the local police force. When I was about to do that, I came out of my house only to come across a police car parked in front of my street. I was shocked. I couldn't believe how expeditious they were, coming to protect me. However, I was told that there was a criminal complaint against me submitted by seven citizens, claiming that I threatened to kill them, brandishing a weapon. They asked me whether I had a weapon. I showed them and showed my license for carrying a weapon. They confiscated the weapon and never returned it to me. After that, I was taken into the police station, interviewed for some two hours, and then a criminal complaint was filed against me by an inspector or a prosecutor. As for my complaint, it remained in a drawer. And when the trial started, I had to file a private suit against people who had evicted me from commercial premises. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you that for some of the complaints, nothing was done, but in this case the prosecutor did do something. There is a victim with the same name as yours. However, the first name is Kristijan. Is he a relative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean -- that's my son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your son was interviewed, because in the prosecutor's report, the statement of your son is mentioned, so you knew -- you knew that there had been a serious investigation and that following that investigation, the prosecutor had information about your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I don't know what situation you have in mind. Which particular case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kristijan Ejic, you said he's your son, was heard as a witness in that particular case. About Josip Bagi, Rade Cakmak and so on, so there was an investigation carried out by the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, nothing escapes me, I see everything, and I noticed that there had been an investigation. So, yes, indeed, maybe some prosecutors put some complaints in the drawers, as you say, but other prosecutors did take action. This prosecutor recorded dozens of victims and prepared an indictment which contains the list of all the victims, so he did his job in 1992, since the indictment bears the date of September, 15th of September, 1992. That's all I wanted to comment upon with you. You've just confirmed that your son was interviewed as a witness and that Mr. Sibincic was charged and sentenced. Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that to fully understand the document that we have already tendered the judgement regarding this trial against Ostoja Sibincic and Rade Cakmak, now the Prosecutor asked to tender into evidence also this document, the indictment that you have discussed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have an exhibit number for P7271.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit P560.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit earlier, the Prosecutor said that he did not intend to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but now he's tendered that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honour, also to be clear, these last three documents, number -- the indictment, that is, number 7271, and the last two articles, number 7270 and 7272, are not still included in the Prosecution exhibit list, so I request to add these three documents to the Prosecution exhibit list, due to their relevance and probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber also rises, Prosecution, to add these three documents onto its exhibit list. Let me remind you that as far as document 7272 is concerned, we have already given it an MFI number. We are awaiting the entire article.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And another [indiscernible] on the line -- on page 38, line 5, this article is indicated as published in July 1993, but it's 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, last few questions. Did you suffer any kind of a persecution for your position regarding these facts that you described today -- in these two days?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have mentioned earlier in my evidence, there was a setup. I was falsely accused when I was evicted from commercial premises. There were proceedings that lasted for a long time, and in the end, to my great joy and pleasure, certain individuals who had accused me, and they were and are to this day members of the Serbian Radical Party, they changed their statement and confessed in court that they had done it for political reasons, that they practically had lied, that it only seemed to them that I had threatened them. Since this suit lasted for a long time and I was harassed, I was visited every two weeks by members of the State Security who interviewed me, and there was also an accusation by Sibincic when his car was blown up, and there was a group of people, and I was a member of that group, who opposed everything, and Sibincic accused that group of that crime. All of us were arrested and taken to the police station. We were kept there the entire night and interviewed. They even brought in an expert with a lie detector from Novi Sad. In the end, they released all of us, having realised, I guess, that it was all false. Following that event, I also had constant visits by members of the State Security. I was frequently searched by police. On one occasion, even a police commander came with two police vehicles early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did they find something relevant in your house when they searched you -- your house?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time when they carried out a search, they found several copies -- or, rather, several bullets from my weapon that had remained in a drawer in my room. These bullets had not been confiscated on the occasion when my pistol was confiscated. They also found an air gun which had a sniper on it. They abused it. It was abused by Vukelja and others, who gave a statement saying that a sniper had been found in my house, without clarifying that it was actually an air gun. As a result of that, I had threats by the villagers who were saying, "Aleksa Ejic has a sniper and intends to use it against refugees." In the end, I was forced -- I apologise. Forgive me. I was forced to travel to the South African Republic, which was the only country where one could travel at the time with a tourist visa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, if you feel emotional about this, we can stop for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am a bit distressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you like us to have a short break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a ten-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Court is back in session. Do you feel better, Witness? Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I feel better now. We can continue. I would just like to ask you for something. If possible, could you avoid questions in relation to my family? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If there are any questions that concern your family, we shall move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, I don't think I have further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ferrara. My colleague would like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, we have been speaking at several occasions about Mr. Sibincic and Mr. Cakmak and others who were active in Hrtkovci in May 1992, and my question to you is if you know whether these gentlemen were members of the SRS, the Serb Radical Party, or if they became members of the SRS, or if they had any particular relation with that party in the time when these events occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at the time when these events occurred, I am not aware of these persons having been members of the Serb Radical Party. Now, whether they had any direct contacts, I am not aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And do you know if, at any later point in time, they became members of the SRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that I do know in relation to one of these persons, Sibincic. Today he is a member of the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you happen to know when he became a member of the SRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it was this year. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And my final question: Do you know if any of these gentlemen that we have been mentioning here had an affiliation with another political party around the time when the events occurred in 1992? I mean either a political party or a political movement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ostoja Sibincic was in the Serbian Renewal Movement, together with me, at first when these events took place in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a question for you. I would first like to read out to you paragraph 124 of the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. This is what the Prosecution says: "Inter-ethnic tension in Hrtkovci increased in 1991, when the first Serbian refugees started arriving from Croatia. The SRS was in charge of their transport aboard buses to Vojvodina. These refugees needed to report to Ostoja Sibincic, a member of the SRS and associate of Vojislav Seselj in Hrtkovci, since he gave them the addresses of houses belonging to Croats. In some cases, owners were abroad and the refugees settled in their houses. In other cases, the refugees threatened them to force them to exchange their homes with those of the refugees in Croatia." What the Prosecution is saying is that Sibincic was a member of the SRS when the refugees arrived. This is why the question put by my colleague is so important. I think we have to -- we need to be clear on this. At what time exactly did you learn that Sibincic, who is a member of the SRS today -- what I'm interested in is to know whether he was at the time a member of the SRS. At what time, if ever he was a member of the SRS at the time, that is, because the Prosecution ascertains that he was a member. When the refugees arrived he was a member.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not aware of that, whether he was a member earlier on. What I know today is that he is a member now, that he joined this year or the end of last year. I cannot give you the exact date. At the time when the refugees were coming in, I don't know, maybe he was a member, but I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that you know that he is a member of the SRS today, and you add that this occurred at the end of last year or the beginning of this year. Is this because he told you that he's now a member of the SRS and he showed you his card? How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I know that on the basis of the statement made by Zeljko Dosen, the president of the local council, and Krasic, Slobodan, my neighbour who told me about that, and I also heard about it from him personally at a meeting this year, when St. Ilija's Day was celebrated. That is the patron saint of our village. So I heard from him personally that he was a member of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992, you can't say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: You left for South Africa. Can you tell me at exactly what time you left, the month and the year, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] April 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think somewhat more than three months. My first visa was for somewhat less than three months, and then in the town of Springs I extended my visa for another month. If you need more precise information than that, I have my old passport of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia with which I can document that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand right, you returned in July or August, you returned home, and when you came back, was everything all right? You didn't encounter any problems? You weren't threatened or accused of anything? Was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, after my return, I did not have any major problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall now have the cross-examination, which will last three hours. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor, and this will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ejic, since when have you been a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. -- Dr. Vojislav Seselj, I have been a member since the local council was established in 1991 or 1992. I don't know exactly. I think it was 1991, the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, could all of the microphones please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I was a member until the local committee was disbanded. After that, I wasn't a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Can you recall the month in which the local committee of the SPO was established in Hrtkovci? That was in 1991? If you cannot, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You did know at the time that the SPO was still a markedly nationalist party?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It started out as the most extreme nationalist party on the Serbian political scene; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Which one was more extreme?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the Serb Chetnik Movement and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why was the Serb Chetnik Movement more extreme?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the main difference is in the fact that the SPO advocated the promotion of nationalist tradition without jeopardising other ethnicities, and it is my opinion that the other movement I referred to did not advocate that. Rather, through volunteers, they provided support for participating in conflicts in Croatia and Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the SPO send volunteers to these conflicts?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SPO did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was the name of the paramilitary formation of the SPO?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called "The Serbian Guard."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A few moments ago, in response to the question put by the Presiding Judge as to whether you had ever heard of the Serbian Guard, why did you say that you had never heard of it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I didn't know which guard this pertained to. Perhaps it was some other Serbian Guard, not the guard of the SPO that I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The logical answer to the Presiding Judge's question could be which Serbian Guard do you have in mind or there are a few Serbian Guards, so let's see which one it could be; right? You cannot say that you haven't heard of the Serbian Guard; am I not right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that Vuk Draskovic, together with his wife, Danica, published the newspaper "The Serbian Word," "Srpska Rec," for years?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was a typical news magazine that came out twice a month?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that in this newspaper, on the front page Vuk Draskovic published a map in colour of an ethnic delineation of Yugoslavia which actually coincides with the map of a Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on some occasion I did see that, too, but I'm not aware of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Vuk Draskovic was one of the most prominent Serb nationalists in the 1980s, after he published his famous novels, "The Knife" and "The Prayer," respectively?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you put a simpler question to me? Could you explain to me what it is you mean by "Serb nationalism"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, a Serb nationalist is a man who fights for the interests of his nation, for national emancipation, for the protection of those parts of his nation that are in jeopardy. That would be it. In the simplest possible terms, that is to say, a person who cares about his people and strives for its interests.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to your question would be the following: When Vuk Draskovic, as a Serb nationalistic, advocated the promotion of positive Serb traditions, not those of the Chetnik Movement or Draza Mihajlovic and others during the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, who erected the single movement that exists until now to Draza Mihajlovic in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Renewal Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Vuk Draskovic, its long-term president?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Vuk Draskovic, it was the SPO and he is the president of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, wasn't he the main initiator within that party to erect this monument?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Vuk Draskovic give an enormous contribution to the rehabilitation the role of General Draza Mihajlovic in the Second World War; is that not an objective fact?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Vuk Draskovic write a novel about the last days of General Draza Mihajlovic? His title is "The General"?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about it. I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So therefore, Vuk Draskovic renewed the traditions of the Chetnik Movement of the Second World War, the Chetnik Movement of Draza Mihajlovic; right?
